submitted.rationale: EQE was highest at the most Fe-rich composition (Fe0.87Sb0.13: 0.637%), which behaves like Sb-doped hematite. EQE fell as Sb increased: 0.294% at 20% Sb and 0.003% at rutile FeSbO4 (48% Sb). MACE puts both hematite and FeSbO4 on the hull. MEGNet predicts gaps at or below 2.7 eV for both, so both phases should absorb; the difference comes from how well each converts light into current, not from absorption.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE of 0.003%. Near-single-phase FeSbO4 absorbs but converts poorly.
Measured EQE of 0.29%, lower than index 0. EQE drops as Sb increases.
It lies between two measured points on a falling trend toward the poor FeSbO4 region, so its expected EQE is low.

consultations.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet HSE gaps: FeSbO4 2.08 eV, hematite 2.77 eV (MEGNet-HSE tends to overestimate; experimental ~2.1 eV), FeSb2O6 1.28 eV. All at or below the 2.7 eV photon energy, so each phase should absorb. Index 4 (20% Sb) should be a hematite/FeSbO4 mixture, possibly with Sb-doped hematite, which is a known good photoanode motif. The gaps alone don't separate the candidates, so I'm treating this as a first probe of the Fe-rich side.

Support. MACE puts rutile FeSbO4 on the hull (0.002 eV/atom above it), so it is the stable ternary phase and index 14 (48% Sb) should be close to single-phase FeSbO4. Its MEGNet gap of 2.08 eV is below the 2.7 eV photons, so it can absorb. Measuring here tests the ternary against the Fe-rich result (0.29%).

Support. MACE puts hematite on the hull (0.0 eV/atom). The measurements so far show that merit comes from the hematite-rich side: 0.29% at 20% Sb against 0.003% at FeSbO4. Index 0 (12.8% Sb) has the most hematite-like, lightly Sb-doped composition, so I pick it over the GP's exploratory choice of index 8, which moves toward the poor FeSbO4 region.
